* ➖ Vendor Click and streamline Typer's functionality and code base. PR [#1774](https://github.com/fastapi/typer/pull/1774) by [@svlandeg](https://github.com/svlandeg).
* Typer no longer depends on Click as a third party dependency, it vendors (includes the source code of) Click.
* This simplifies the work done by both Click and Typer teams.
* It allows Typer to evolve independently, and enables several new planned features.
* It will solve several dependency conflict situations for projects that use some packages that depend on Click and some that depend on Typer.
* This also means that Click-specific functionality is no longer supported, like extracting the Click app and adding Click-specific plug-ins, or customizing the field types with Click-specific types.
* You can read more about it in the docs for [Vendored Click](https://typer.tiangolo.com/tutorial/click/).

* 🔥 Remove auto naming of groups added via `add_typer` based on the group's callback function name. PR [#1052](https://github.com/fastapi/typer/pull/1052) by [@patrick91](https://github.com/patrick91).
Before, it was supported to infer the name of a command group from the callback function name in the sub-app, so, in this code:
def users():  # <-- This was the inferred command group name
...the command group would be named `users`, based on the name of the function `def users()`.
Now you need to set it explicitly:
app.add_typer(users_app, name="users")  # <-- Explicitly set the command group name
**Note**: this change will enable important features in the next release. 🤩

Now you don't need to install `typer[all]`. When you install `typer` it comes with the default optional dependencies and the `typer` command.
If you don't want the extra optional dependencies (`rich` and `shellingham`), you can install `typer-slim` instead.
You can also install `typer-slim[standard]`, which includes the default optional dependencies, but not the `typer` command.

Now the package `typer-cli` doesn't add anything on top of what `typer` has, it only depends on `typer`, and is there only for backwards compatibility, so that projects that depend on `typer-cli` can get the latest features of the `typer` command while they upgrade their dependencies to require `typer` directly.
* ✨ Add support for `typer ./someprogram.py utils docs --title`. PR [#782](https://github.com/tiangolo/typer/pull/782) by [@tiangolo](https://github.com/tiangolo).

* 🐛 Fix broken installation when upgrading from `typer <0.12.0` to `typer >=0.12.0`, make `typer` independent of `typer-slim`, include `typer` command in `typer` package. PR [#791](https://github.com/tiangolo/typer/pull/791) by [@tiangolo](https://github.com/tiangolo).
This fixes a problem that would break the `typer` installation directory when upgrading from `typer <0.12.0` to `typer >=0.12.0`, see issue [#790](https://github.com/tiangolo/typer/issues/790).
By installing the latest version (`0.12.1`) it fixes it, for any previous version, even if the installation directory was already broken by the previous upgrade.

In version `0.12.0`, the `typer` package depends on `typer-slim[standard]` which includes the default dependencies (instead of `typer[all]`) and `typer-cli` (that provides the `typer` command).
If you don't want the extra optional dependencies (`rich` and `shellingham`), you can install `typer-slim` instead.
You can also install `typer-slim[standard]`, which includes the default optional dependencies, but not the `typer` command.
In version `0.12.0` the `typer-cli` package only provides the `typer` command, but the code is still in the main code, so even without installing `typer-cli`, it can be called with `python -m typer`.

This approach of having `typer` depend on `typer-slim[standard]` instead of including the whole code and dependencies itself caused an issue when upgrading from `typer <0.12.0` to `typer >=0.12.0`, see issue [#790](https://github.com/tiangolo/typer/issues/790). This is fixed in version `0.12.1`.

This release adds deep integrations with [Rich](https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/stable/). ✨
`rich` is an optional dependency, you can install it directly or it will be included when you install with:
If Rich is available, it will be used to show the content from `--help` options, validation errors, and even errors in your app (exception tracebacks).
There are new options to group commands, *CLI arguments*, and *CLI options*, support for [Rich Console Markup](https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/stable/markup.html), and more! 🎉

The same as before, you can add help for the commands in the docstrings and the *CLI options*.
And the `typer.Typer()` application receives a parameter `help` that you can pass with the main help text for your CLI program:
--install-completion  Install completion for the current shell.
--show-completion     Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or customize the installation.
create      Create a new user with username.
delete      Delete a user with username.
delete-all  Delete ALL users in the database.
// Now the commands have inline help 🎉
Create a new user with username.
If --force is not used, will ask for confirmation.
Delete ALL users in the database.
If --force is not used, will ask for confirmation.
`typer.Typer()` receives several other parameters for other things, we'll see that later.
You will also see how to use "Callbacks" later, and those include a way to add this same help message in a function docstring.

You will probably be better adding the help text as a docstring to your functions, but if for some reason you wanted to overwrite it, you can use the `help` function argument passed to `@app.command()`:
// Notice it uses the help passed to @app.command()
--install-completion  Install completion for the current shell.
--show-completion     Show completion for the current shell, to copy
create  Create a new user with username.
delete  Delete a user with username.
// It uses "Create a new user with username." instead of "Some internal utility function to create."
There could be cases where you have a command in your app that you need to deprecate, so that your users stop using it, even while it's still supported for a while.

The main visual difference between a *CLI option* and a *CLI argument* is that the *CLI option* has `--` prepended to the name, like in "`--size`".

A *CLI option* doesn't depend on the order because it has a predefined name (here it's `--size`). This is because the CLI app is looking specifically for a literal `--size` parameter (also known as "flag" or "switch"), with that specific "name" (here the specific name is "`--size`"). The CLI app will check if you typed it or not, it will be actively looking for `--size` even if you didn't type it (to check if it's there or not).

In contrast, the CLI app is not actively looking for the *CLI argument* with a text "`./myproject`", it has no way to know if you would type `./myproject` or `./my-super-awesome-project` or anything else. It's just waiting to get whatever you give it. The only way to know that you refer to a specific *CLI argument* is because of the order. The same way that it knows that the first *CLI argument* was the `name` and the second was the `lastname`, but if you mixed the order, it wouldn't be able to handle it.
Instead, with a *CLI option*, the order doesn't matter.
Also, by default, a *CLI option* is *optional* (not *required*).
But the *required* and *optional* defaults can be changed.
So, the main and **most important** difference is that:
* *CLI options* **start with `--`** and don't depend on the order
In this example above the *CLI option* `--size` is just a "flag" or "switch" that will contain a boolean value, `True` or `False`, depending on if it was added to the command or not.
This one doesn't receive any values. But *CLI options* can also receive values like *CLI arguments*. You'll see how later.

Be aware that these terms refer to multiple things depending on the context, and sadly, those "contexts" mix frequently, so it's easy to get confused.
In Python, the names of the variables in a function, like `name` and `lastname`:
are called "Python function parameters" or "Python function arguments".
There's actually a very small distinction in Python between "parameter" and "argument".
It's quite technical... and somewhat pedantic.
*Parameter* refers to the variable name in a function *declaration*. Like:
*Argument* refers to the value passed when *calling* a function. Like:
...but you will probably see them used interchangeably in most of the places (including here).
In Python, in a function, a parameter with a *default value* like `lastname` in:
The default value can be anything, like `""` or `None`.
And a parameter like `name`, that doesn't have a default value, is considered *required*.
When talking about command line interface applications, the words **"argument"** and **"parameter"** are commonly used to refer to that data passed to a CLI app, those parameters.
But those words **don't imply** anything about the data being required, needing to be passed in a certain order, nor having a flag like `--lastname`.

The parameters that come with a name like `--lastname` (and optionally a value) are commonly optional, not required. So, when talking about CLIs it's common to call them **optional arguments** or **optional parameters**. Sometimes these *optional parameters* that start with `--` are also called a **flag** or a **switch**.
In reality, the parameters that require an order can be made *optional* too. And the ones that come with a flag (like `--lastname`) can be *required* too.
To try and make it a bit easier, we'll normally use the words "parameter" or "argument" to refer to "Python functions parameters" or "Python functions arguments".
We'll use ***CLI argument*** to refer to those *CLI parameters* that depend on the specific order. That are **required** by default.
And we'll use ***CLI option*** to refer to those *CLI parameters* that depend on a name that starts with `--` (like `--lastname`). That are **optional** by default.
We will use ***CLI parameter*** to refer to both, *CLI arguments* and *CLI options*.

Typer, build great CLIs. Easy to code. Based on Python type hints.

Typer is a library for building <abbr title="command line interface, programs executed from a terminal">CLI</abbr> applications that users will **love using** and developers will **love creating**. Based on Python type hints.
It's also a command line tool to run scripts, automatically converting them to CLI applications.

* **Intuitive to write**: Great editor support. <abbr title="also known as auto-complete, autocompletion, IntelliSense">Completion</abbr> everywhere. Less time debugging. Designed to be easy to use and learn. Less time reading docs.
* **Easy to use**: It's easy to use for the final users. Automatic help, and automatic completion for all shells.
* **Short**: Minimize code duplication. Multiple features from each parameter declaration. Fewer bugs.
* **Start simple**: The simplest example adds only 2 lines of code to your app: **1 import, 1 function call**.
* **Grow large**: Grow in complexity as much as you want, create arbitrarily complex trees of commands and groups of subcommands, with options and arguments.
* **Run scripts**: Typer includes a `typer` command/program that you can use to run scripts, automatically converting them to CLIs, even if they don't use Typer internally.
**Typer** is [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com)'s little sibling, it's the FastAPI of CLIs.

**Typer** requires only a few dependencies (most are tiny):
* [`rich`](https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/stable/index.html): to show nicely formatted errors automatically.
* [`shellingham`](https://github.com/sarugaku/shellingham): to automatically detect the current shell when installing completion.
* [`annotated-doc`](https://github.com/fastapi/annotated-doc): to generate documentation from Python type annotations.
* [`colorama`](https://github.com/tartley/colorama) (only on Windows): for producing colored terminal text on Windows.
Typer used to depend on [Click](https://click.palletsprojects.com/) as well, a popular tool for building CLIs in Python.

Since version 0.26.0, Typer has vendored Click (included Click's source code internally, instead of installing it as a third party package) and has unified the code interactions between Typer and the embedded Click source code for easier maintainability in the future.
Note that some Click functionality will not be available anymore in the future, as we continue to improve and extend Typer's codebase.
There used to be a slimmed-down version of Typer called `typer-slim`, which didn't include the dependencies `rich` and `shellingham`, nor the `typer` command.
However, since version 0.22.0, we have stopped supporting this, and `typer-slim` now simply installs (all of) Typer.
If you want to disable Rich globally, you can set an environmental variable `TYPER_USE_RICH` to `False` or `0`.

Typer, build great CLIs. Easy to code. Based on Python type hints.

Typer is a library for building <abbr title="command line interface, programs executed from a terminal">CLI</abbr> applications that users will **love using** and developers will **love creating**. Based on Python type hints.
It's also a command line tool to run scripts, automatically converting them to CLI applications.

* **Intuitive to write**: Great editor support. <abbr title="also known as auto-complete, autocompletion, IntelliSense">Completion</abbr> everywhere. Less time debugging. Designed to be easy to use and learn. Less time reading docs.
* **Easy to use**: It's easy to use for the final users. Automatic help, and automatic completion for all shells.
* **Short**: Minimize code duplication. Multiple features from each parameter declaration. Fewer bugs.
* **Start simple**: The simplest example adds only 2 lines of code to your app: **1 import, 1 function call**.
* **Grow large**: Grow in complexity as much as you want, create arbitrarily complex trees of commands and groups of subcommands, with options and arguments.
* **Run scripts**: Typer includes a `typer` command/program that you can use to run scripts, automatically converting them to CLIs, even if they don't use Typer internally.
**Typer** is [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com)'s little sibling, it's the FastAPI of CLIs.

**Typer** requires only a few dependencies (most are tiny):
* [`rich`](https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/stable/index.html): to show nicely formatted errors automatically.
* [`shellingham`](https://github.com/sarugaku/shellingham): to automatically detect the current shell when installing completion.
* [`annotated-doc`](https://github.com/fastapi/annotated-doc): to generate documentation from Python type annotations.
* [`colorama`](https://github.com/tartley/colorama) (only on Windows): for producing colored terminal text on Windows.
Typer used to depend on [Click](https://click.palletsprojects.com/) as well, a popular tool for building CLIs in Python.

Since version 0.26.0, Typer has vendored Click (included Click's source code internally, instead of installing it as a third party package) and has unified the code interactions between Typer and the embedded Click source code for easier maintainability in the future.
Note that some Click functionality will not be available anymore in the future, as we continue to improve and extend Typer's codebase.
There used to be a slimmed-down version of Typer called `typer-slim`, which didn't include the dependencies `rich` and `shellingham`, nor the `typer` command.
However, since version 0.22.0, we have stopped supporting this, and `typer-slim` now simply installs (all of) Typer.
If you want to disable Rich globally, you can set an environmental variable `TYPER_USE_RICH` to `False` or `0`.

The way printing works underneath is that the **operating system** (Linux, Windows, macOS) treats what we print as if our CLI program was **writing text** to a "**virtual file**" called "**standard output**".
When our code "prints" things it is actually "writing" to this "virtual file" of "standard output".
This might seem strange, but that's how the CLI program and the operating system interact with each other.
And then the operating system **shows on the screen** whatever our CLI program "**wrote**" to that "**virtual file**" called "**standard output**".
And there's another "**virtual file**" called "**standard error**" that is normally only used for errors.
But we can also "print" to "standard error". And both are shown on the terminal to the users.
If you use PowerShell it's quite possible that what you print to "standard error" won't be shown in the terminal.
In PowerShell, to see "standard error" you would have to check the variable `$Error`.
But it will work normally in Bash, Zsh, and Fish.
You can print to "standard error" creating a Rich `Console` with `stderr=True`.
Using `stderr=True` tells **Rich** that the output should be shown in "standard error".
When you try it in the terminal, it will probably just look the same:

As a final detail, when you type text in your keyboard to your terminal, the operating system also considers it another "**virtual file**" that you are writing text to.
This virtual file is called "**standard input**".
Right now this probably seems quite useless 🤷‍♂.
But understanding that will come handy in the future, for example for autocompletion and testing.
In most of the cases, for displaying advanced information, it is recommended to use [Rich](https://rich.readthedocs.io/).

What inspired **Typer**, how it compares to other alternatives and what it learned from them.
**Typer** wouldn't exist if not for the previous work of others.
There have been many tools created before that have helped inspire its creation.
`argparse` is the Python standard library's module to write CLIs.
It provides a better alternative than reading the *CLI Parameters* as a `list` of `str` and parsing everything by hand.
Provide a better development experience than just reading *CLI Parameters* by hand.
Hug is a library to create APIs and CLIs, it uses parameters in functions to declare the required data.
It inspired a lot of the ideas in **FastAPI** and **Typer**.
Use function parameters to declare *CLI arguments* and *CLI options* as it simplifies a lot the development experience.
Plac is another library to create CLIs using parameters in functions, similar to Hug.
Provide a simple way to use a function as a command line app, without having to create a complete app, with `typer.run(some_function)`.
Pydantic is a library to handle data validation using standard modern Python type annotations.
It is not used by **Typer**, but it inspired a lot of the design (through **FastAPI**).
Use standard Python type annotations to declare types instead of library-specific types or classes and use them for data validation and documentation.
Click is one of the most widely used libraries to create CLIs in Python.
It's a very powerful tool and there are many CLIs built with it. It is what powers **Typer** underneath.

It also uses functions with parameters for *CLI arguments* and *CLI options*, but the declaration of the specific *CLI arguments*, *CLI options*, types, etc, is done in decorators on top of the function. This requires some code repetition (e.g. a *CLI Option* name `--verbose` and a variable name `verbose`) and synchronization between two places related to the same information (the decorator and the parameter function).

It uses decorators on top of functions to modify the actual value of those functions, converting them to instances of a specific class. This is a clever trick, but code editors can't provide great support for autocompletion that way.
It was built with some great ideas and design using the features available in the language at the time (Python 2.x).

And now **Typer** improved it to have new features, tests, some bug fixes (for issues in plain `click-completion` and Click), and better support for shells, including modern versions of PowerShell (e.g. the default versions that come with Windows 10).

Typer used to depend on [Click](https://click.palletsprojects.com/), a popular tool for building CLIs in Python, as an external dependency.

Since version 0.26.0, Typer has vendored Click (included Click's source code internally, instead of installing it as a third party package) and has unified the code interactions between Typer and the embedded Click source code for easier maintainability in the future.
Note that some Click functionality will not be available anymore in the future, as we continue to improve and extend Typer's codebase.
Typer used to support extracting the internal Click app from a Typer app to use and modify it with any Click functionality. For example, to add Click-specific plug-ins.
The same way, it supported adding Click-specific types to override the default Typer ones.

Using Click directly was an edge case feature that was not commonly used, and it is no longer supported. If your app depended specifically on this, you will need to either migrate it to use plain Typer, or migrate it to use Click directly instead of Typer.
Because Typer used to depend on Click, any new features or changes in newer Click versions could break compatibility in Typer.
The Click team has always been very helpful and supportive with Typer. But still, this dependency interaction would cause extra effort and burden for both the Typer team and the Click team.
Now that Typer continues evolving, starting from a fixed copy of Click's source code, any changes in Click's codebase will not affect Typer.
The Typer team will not need to make sure there are workarounds for changes in new versions of Click, and the Click team will not need to consider additional edge cases caused by Typer.
The fact that Typer depended on Click caused an additional ongoing issue that could happen from time to time to user projects.
Many packages come with a CLI, some of them could use Click, some could use Typer.
Some of these packages could require a recent version of Click that Typer still didn't support, but as all these package dependencies would belong to the same project, there would be conflicts.

In these cases, the package that depended on the newer version of Click would require installing it, but the other package that used Typer would break. Or if there were version pins, some combinations of packages would not be installable together.
Across different versions of Click through time, there were many changes needed in Typer to make it all compatible with multiple versions of Click at the same time.

Now that Typer and Click are decoupled, a package could depend on a newer version of Click, while another package that uses Typer would continue working as normally, as that Typer version would bundle anything necessary from Click's source code to work.
Both the Click team and the Typer team have future improvements planned, not having to coordinate with each other for compatibility will simplify the work of both teams.
In some cases feature ideas could overlap, and could have caused incompatibilities. Now this won't be a problem as each team can focus on each project independently.

After vendoring Click, Typer will reduce, simplify and refactor parts of the vendored Click code that are not necessary for Typer, or that could be done in a different way to facilitate future improvements in Typer.
Then Typer will gradually introduce new features and improvements that have been planned for a while but were too difficult to implement before this.

These decisions are all carefully planned and based on real world use cases extracted from the official Typer developer survey, including the tradeoff between the potential breaking changes for some use cases and the planned future features and improvements that will be enabled.
Click has been the foundation building block of Typer and most CLI's in Python (through Typer or directly with Click).
We wouldn't be here without Click, and we are very grateful for all the work that the Click team has done.

`uv add typer` installs both the Typer library and the `typer` command in the project's `.venv`.

**Typer** was designed to be easy and intuitive to use, to ensure the best development experience. With autocompletion everywhere.

Here's how your editor might help you:

It could be that your code determined that the program completed successfully, or it could be an operation aborted.

You can normally just let the code of your CLI program finish its execution, but in some scenarios, you might want to terminate at some point in the middle of it. And prevent any subsequent code to run.
This doesn't have to mean that there's an error, just that nothing else needs to be executed.
In that case, you can raise a `typer.Exit()` exception:
There are several things to see in this example.
* The CLI program is the function `main()`, not the others. This is the one that takes a *CLI argument*.
* The function `maybe_create_user()` can terminate the program by raising `typer.Exit()`.
* If the program is terminated by `maybe_create_user()` then `send_new_user_notification()` will never execute inside of `main()`.

// Notice that the notification code was never run, the second message is not printed
Even though you are raising an exception, it doesn't necessarily mean there's an error.
This is done with an exception because it works as an "error" and stops all execution.
But then **Typer** catches it and just terminates the program normally.
`typer.Exit()` takes an optional `code` parameter. By default, `code` is `0`, meaning there was no error.
You can pass a `code` with a number other than `0` to tell the terminal that there was an error in the execution of the program:

// Print the result code of the last program executed
// 1 means there was an error, 0 means no errors.
The error code might be used by other programs (for example a Bash script) that execute your CLI program.
There's a special exception that you can use to "abort" a program.
It works more or less the same as `typer.Exit()` but will print `"Aborted!"` to the screen and can be useful in certain cases later to make it explicit that the execution was aborted:

And your editor (and **Typer**) will know that:

* `formal` is a `bool` and is by default `False`.
* `intro` is an optional `str`, by default is `None`.
These type hints are what give you autocomplete in your editor and several other features.
**Typer** is based on these type hints.
This tutorial shows you how to use **Typer** with all its features, step by step.

100|            )
101|            for d in default_value
102|        ]
103|        if all(not part for part in parts):

105|        else:

107|    elif isinstance(default_value, Enum):

61|def except_hook(
62|    exc_type: type[BaseException], exc_value: BaseException, tb: TracebackType | None
63|) -> None:
64|    exception_config: DeveloperExceptionConfig | None = getattr(
65|        exc_value, _typer_developer_exception_attr_name, None
66|    )
67|    standard_traceback = os.getenv(
68|        "TYPER_STANDARD_TRACEBACK", os.getenv("_TYPER_STANDARD_TRACEBACK")
69|    )
70|    if (
71|        standard_traceback
72|        or not exception_config
73|        or not exception_config.pretty_exceptions_enable
74|    ):
75|        _original_except_hook(exc_type, exc_value, tb)
76|        return
77|    typer_path = os.path.dirname(__file__)
78|    click_path = os.path.dirname(_click.__file__)
79|    internal_dir_names = [typer_path, click_path]
80|    exc = exc_value
81|    if HAS_RICH:
82|        from . import rich_utils
83|
84|        rich_tb = rich_utils.get_traceback(exc, exception_config, internal_dir_names)
85|        console_stderr = rich_utils._get_rich_console(stderr=True)
86|        console_stderr.print(rich_tb)
87|        return
88|    tb_exc = traceback.TracebackException.from_exception(exc)
89|    stack: list[FrameSummary] = []
90|    for frame in tb_exc.stack:
91|        if any(frame.filename.startswith(path) for path in internal_dir_names):
92|            if not exception_config.pretty_exceptions_short:
93|                # Hide the line for internal libraries, Typer and Click
94|                stack.append(
95|                    traceback.FrameSummary(
96|                        filename=frame.filename,
97|                        lineno=frame.lineno,
98|                        name=frame.name,
99|                        line="",
100|                    )
101|                )
102|        else:
103|            stack.append(frame)
104|    # Type ignore ref: https://github.com/python/typeshed/pull/8244
105|    final_stack_summary = StackSummary.from_list(stack)
106|    tb_exc.stack = final_stack_summary
107|    for line in tb_exc.format():
108|        print(line, file=sys.stderr)
109|    return

1211|def solve_typer_info_help(typer_info: TyperInfo) -> str:
1212|    # Priority 1: Explicit value was set in app.add_typer()
1213|    if not isinstance(typer_info.help, DefaultPlaceholder):
1214|        return inspect.cleandoc(typer_info.help or "")
1215|    # Priority 2: Explicit value was set in sub_app.callback()
1216|    if typer_info.typer_instance and typer_info.typer_instance.registered_callback:
1217|        callback_help = typer_info.typer_instance.registered_callback.help
1218|        if not isinstance(callback_help, DefaultPlaceholder):
1219|            return inspect.cleandoc(callback_help or "")
1220|    # Priority 3: Explicit value was set in sub_app = typer.Typer()
1221|    if typer_info.typer_instance and typer_info.typer_instance.info:
1222|        instance_help = typer_info.typer_instance.info.help
1223|        if not isinstance(instance_help, DefaultPlaceholder):
1224|            return inspect.cleandoc(instance_help or "")
1225|    # Priority 4: Implicit inference from callback docstring in app.add_typer()
1226|    if typer_info.callback:
1227|        doc = inspect.getdoc(typer_info.callback)
1228|        if doc:
1229|            return doc
1230|    # Priority 5: Implicit inference from callback docstring in @app.callback()
1231|    if typer_info.typer_instance and typer_info.typer_instance.registered_callback:
1232|        callback = typer_info.typer_instance.registered_callback.callback
1233|        if not isinstance(callback, DefaultPlaceholder):
1234|            doc = inspect.getdoc(callback or "")
1235|            if doc:
1236|                return doc
1237|    # Priority 6: Implicit inference from callback docstring in typer.Typer()
1238|    if typer_info.typer_instance and typer_info.typer_instance.info:
1239|        instance_callback = typer_info.typer_instance.info.callback
1240|        if not isinstance(instance_callback, DefaultPlaceholder):
1241|            doc = inspect.getdoc(instance_callback)
1242|            if doc:
1243|                return doc
1244|    # Value not set, use the default
1245|    return typer_info.help.value

1248|def solve_typer_info_defaults(typer_info: TyperInfo) -> TyperInfo:
1249|    values: dict[str, Any] = {}
1250|    for name, value in typer_info.__dict__.items():
1251|        # Priority 1: Value was set in app.add_typer()
1252|        if not isinstance(value, DefaultPlaceholder):
1253|            values[name] = value
1254|            continue
1255|        # Priority 2: Value was set in @subapp.callback()
1256|        try:
1257|            callback_value = getattr(
1258|                typer_info.typer_instance.registered_callback,  # type: ignore
1259|                name,
1260|            )
1261|            if not isinstance(callback_value, DefaultPlaceholder):
1262|                values[name] = callback_value
1263|                continue
1264|        except AttributeError:
1265|            pass
1266|        # Priority 3: Value set in subapp = typer.Typer()
1267|        try:
1268|            instance_value = getattr(
1269|                typer_info.typer_instance.info,  # type: ignore
1270|                name,
1271|            )
1272|            if not isinstance(instance_value, DefaultPlaceholder):
1273|                values[name] = instance_value
1274|                continue
1275|        except AttributeError:
1276|            pass
1277|        # Value not set, use the default
1278|        values[name] = value.value
1279|    values["help"] = solve_typer_info_help(typer_info)
1280|    return TyperInfo(**values)

1439|    if lenient_issubclass(type_, Path):

1446|def param_path_convertor(value: str | None = None) -> Path | None:
1447|    if value is not None:
1448|        # allow returning any subclass of Path created by an annotated parser without converting
1449|        # it back to a Path
1450|        return value if isinstance(value, Path) else Path(value)

1454|def generate_enum_convertor(enum: type[Enum]) -> Callable[[Any], Any]:
1455|    val_map = {str(val.value): val for val in enum}
1456|
1457|    def convertor(value: Any) -> Any:
1458|        if value is not None:
1459|            val = str(value)
1460|            if val in val_map:
1461|                key = val_map[val]
1462|                return enum(key)
1463|
1464|    return convertor

1467|def generate_list_convertor(
1468|    convertor: Callable[[Any], Any] | None, default_value: Any | None
1469|) -> Callable[[Sequence[Any] | None], list[Any] | None]:
1470|    def internal_convertor(value: Sequence[Any] | None) -> list[Any] | None:
1471|        if (value is None) or (default_value is None and len(value) == 0):
1472|            return None
1473|        return [convertor(v) if convertor else v for v in value]
1474|
1475|    return internal_convertor

1478|def generate_tuple_convertor(
1479|    types: Sequence[Any],
1480|) -> Callable[[tuple[Any, ...] | None], tuple[Any, ...] | None]:
1481|    convertors = [determine_type_convertor(type_) for type_ in types]
1482|
1483|    def internal_convertor(
1484|        param_args: tuple[Any, ...] | None,
1485|    ) -> tuple[Any, ...] | None:
1486|        if param_args is None:
1487|            return None
1488|        return tuple(
1489|            convertor(arg) if convertor else arg
1490|            for (convertor, arg) in zip(convertors, param_args, strict=False)
1491|        )
1492|
1493|    return internal_convertor

1496|def get_callback(
1497|    *,
1498|    callback: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
1499|    params: Sequence[_click.Parameter] = [],
1500|    convertors: dict[str, Callable[[str], Any]] | None = None,
1501|    context_param_name: str | None = None,
1502|    pretty_exceptions_short: bool,
1503|) -> Callable[..., Any] | None:
1504|    use_convertors = convertors or {}
1505|    if not callback:
1506|        return None
1507|    parameters = get_params_from_function(callback)
1508|    use_params: dict[str, Any] = {}
1509|    for param_name in parameters:
1510|        use_params[param_name] = None
1511|    for param in params:
1512|        if param.name:
1513|            use_params[param.name] = param.default
1514|
1515|    def wrapper(**kwargs: Any) -> Any:
1516|        _rich_traceback_guard = pretty_exceptions_short  # noqa: F841
1517|        for k, v in kwargs.items():
1518|            if k in use_convertors:
1519|                use_params[k] = use_convertors[k](v)
1520|            else:
1521|                use_params[k] = v
1522|        if context_param_name:
1523|            use_params[context_param_name] = get_current_context()
1524|        return callback(**use_params)
1525|
1526|    update_wrapper(wrapper, callback)
1527|    return wrapper

1638|    # * required

1642|        parameter_info = param.default
1643|        if parameter_info.default == Required:
1644|            required = True
1645|        else:
1646|            default_value = parameter_info.default
1647|    elif param.default == Required or param.default is param.empty:
1648|        required = True
1649|        parameter_info = ArgumentInfo()
1650|    else:
1651|        default_value = param.default
1652|        parameter_info = OptionInfo()
1653|    annotation: Any
1654|    if param.annotation is not param.empty:
1655|        annotation = param.annotation
1656|    else:
1657|        annotation = str
1658|    main_type = annotation
1659|    is_list = False
1660|    is_tuple = False
1661|    parameter_type: Any = None
1662|    is_flag = None

1664|
1665|    if origin is not None:
1666|        # Handle SomeType | None and Optional[SomeType]
1667|        if is_union(origin):
1668|            types = []
1669|            for type_ in get_args(main_type):
1670|                if type_ is NoneType:
1671|                    continue
1672|                types.append(type_)
1673|            assert len(types) == 1, "Typer Currently doesn't support Union types"
1674|            main_type = types[0]
1675|            origin = get_origin(main_type)
1676|        # Handle Tuples and Lists
1677|        if lenient_issubclass(origin, list):
1678|            main_type = get_args(main_type)[0]
1679|            assert not get_origin(main_type), (
1680|                "List types with complex sub-types are not currently supported"
1681|            )
1682|            is_list = True
1683|        elif lenient_issubclass(origin, tuple):
1684|            types = []
1685|            for type_ in get_args(main_type):
1686|                assert not get_origin(type_), (
1687|                    "Tuple types with complex sub-types are not currently supported"
1688|                )
1689|                types.append(
1690|                    get_click_type(annotation=type_, parameter_info=parameter_info)
1691|                )
1692|            parameter_type = tuple(types)
1693|            is_tuple = True
1694|    if parameter_type is None:
1695|        parameter_type = get_click_type(
1696|            annotation=main_type, parameter_info=parameter_info
1697|        )
1698|    convertor = determine_type_convertor(main_type)
1699|    if is_list:
1700|        convertor = generate_list_convertor(
1701|            convertor=convertor, default_value=default_value

1703|    if is_tuple:

1712|            param.name, parameter_info.metavar
1713|        )
1714|        if is_flag:

1717|            )
1718|        else:
1719|            default_option_declaration = f"--{default_option_name}"

1726|            TyperOption(

1728|                param_decls=param_decls,

1739|                help=parameter_info.help,
1740|                hidden=parameter_info.hidden,

1797|def get_param_callback(
1798|    *,
1799|    callback: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
1800|    convertor: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
1801|) -> Callable[..., Any] | None:
1802|    if not callback:
1803|        return None
1804|    parameters = get_params_from_function(callback)
1805|    ctx_name = None
1806|    click_param_name = None
1807|    value_name = None
1808|    untyped_names: list[str] = []
1809|    for param_name, param_sig in parameters.items():
1810|        if lenient_issubclass(param_sig.annotation, _click.Context):
1811|            ctx_name = param_name
1812|        elif lenient_issubclass(param_sig.annotation, _click.Parameter):
1813|            click_param_name = param_name
1814|        else:
1815|            untyped_names.append(param_name)
1816|    # Extract value param name first
1817|    if untyped_names:
1818|        value_name = untyped_names.pop()
1819|    # If context and Click param were not typed (old/Click callback style) extract them
1820|    if untyped_names:
1821|        if ctx_name is None:
1822|            ctx_name = untyped_names.pop(0)
1823|        if click_param_name is None:
1824|            if untyped_names:
1825|                click_param_name = untyped_names.pop(0)
1826|        if untyped_names:
1827|            raise _click.ClickException(
1828|                "Too many CLI parameter callback function parameters"
1829|            )
1830|
1831|    def wrapper(ctx: _click.Context, param: _click.Parameter, value: Any) -> Any:
1832|        use_params: dict[str, Any] = {}
1833|        if ctx_name:
1834|            use_params[ctx_name] = ctx
1835|        if click_param_name:
1836|            use_params[click_param_name] = param
1837|        if value_name:
1838|            if convertor:
1839|                use_value = convertor(value)
1840|            else:
1841|                use_value = value
1842|            use_params[value_name] = use_value
1843|        return callback(**use_params)
1844|
1845|    update_wrapper(wrapper, callback)
1846|    return wrapper

1852|    if not callback:
1853|        return None
1854|    parameters = get_params_from_function(callback)
1855|    ctx_name = None
1856|    args_name = None
1857|    incomplete_name = None

1859|    for param_sig in unassigned_params[:]:
1860|        origin = get_origin(param_sig.annotation)

1862|            ctx_name = param_sig.name
1863|            unassigned_params.remove(param_sig)
1864|        elif lenient_issubclass(origin, list):
1865|            args_name = param_sig.name
1866|            unassigned_params.remove(param_sig)
1867|        elif lenient_issubclass(param_sig.annotation, str):
1868|            incomplete_name = param_sig.name
1869|            unassigned_params.remove(param_sig)
1870|    # If there are still unassigned parameters (not typed), extract by name
1871|    for param_sig in unassigned_params[:]:

1873|            ctx_name = param_sig.name
1874|            unassigned_params.remove(param_sig)
1875|        elif args_name is None and param_sig.name == "args":
1876|            args_name = param_sig.name
1877|            unassigned_params.remove(param_sig)
1878|        elif incomplete_name is None and param_sig.name == "incomplete":

581|class Tuple(CompositeParamType):
582|    """The default behavior of Click is to apply a type on a value directly.
583|    This works well in most cases, except for when `nargs` is set to a fixed
584|    count and different types should be used for different items.  In this
585|    case the `Tuple` type can be used.  This type can only be used
586|    if `nargs` is set to a fixed number.

588|    For more information see `tuple-type`.
589|
590|    This can be selected by using a Python tuple literal as a type.
591|    """

593|    def __init__(self, types: Sequence[type[Any] | ParamType]) -> None:
594|        self.types: Sequence[ParamType] = [convert_type(ty) for ty in types]
595|
596|    @property
597|    def name(self) -> str:  # type: ignore[override]
598|        return f"<{' '.join(ty.name for ty in self.types)}>"
599|
600|    @property
601|    def arity(self) -> int:  # type: ignore
602|        return len(self.types)

604|    def convert(
605|        self, value: Any, param: Union["Parameter", None], ctx: Union["Context", None]
606|    ) -> Any:
607|        len_type = len(self.types)
608|        len_value = len(value)
609|
610|        if len_value != len_type:
611|            self.fail(
612|                f"{len_type} values are required, but {len_value} given.",
613|                param=param,
614|                ctx=ctx,

622|def convert_type(ty: Any | None, default: Any | None = None) -> ParamType:
623|    """Find the most appropriate `ParamType` for the given Python
624|    type. If the type isn't provided, it can be inferred from a default
625|    value.
626|    """
627|    guessed_type = False
628|
629|    if ty is None and default is not None:
630|        if isinstance(default, (tuple, list)):
631|            # If the default is empty, ty will remain None and will
632|            # return STRING.
633|            if default:
634|                item = default[0]
635|
636|                # A tuple of tuples needs to detect the inner types.
637|                # Can't call convert recursively because that would
638|                # incorrectly unwind the tuple to a single type.
639|                if isinstance(item, (tuple, list)):
640|                    ty = tuple(map(type, item))
641|                else:
642|                    ty = type(item)
643|        else:
644|            ty = type(default)
645|
646|        guessed_type = True
647|
648|    if isinstance(ty, tuple):
649|        return Tuple(ty)
650|
651|    if isinstance(ty, ParamType):
652|        return ty
653|
654|    if ty is str or ty is None:
655|        return STRING
656|
657|    if ty is int:
658|        return INT
659|
660|    if ty is float:
661|        return FLOAT
662|
663|    if ty is bool:
664|        return BOOL
665|
666|    if guessed_type:
667|        return STRING
668|

267|def _resolve_incomplete(

275|    # as a separate item, or return the split name and value. Always
276|    # split and discard the "=" to make completion easier.
277|    if incomplete == "=":

281|        args.append(name)

285|    # given and the incomplete arg looks like an option, the current
286|    # command will provide option name completions.
287|    if "--" not in args and _start_of_option(ctx, incomplete):

293|    # value, the option will provide value completions.
294|    for param in params:

299|    # parsed value will provide value completions.
300|    for param in params:

61|def make_default_short_help(help: str, max_length: int = 45) -> str:
62|    """Returns a condensed version of help string."""
63|    # Consider only the first paragraph.
64|    paragraph_end = help.find("\n\n")
65|
66|    if paragraph_end != -1:
67|        help = help[:paragraph_end]
68|
69|    # Collapse newlines, tabs, and spaces.
70|    words = help.split()
71|
72|    if not words:
73|        return ""
74|
75|    # The first paragraph started with a "no rewrap" marker, ignore it.
76|    if words[0] == "\b":
77|        words = words[1:]
78|
79|    total_length = 0
80|    last_index = len(words) - 1
81|
82|    for i, word in enumerate(words):
83|        total_length += len(word) + (i > 0)
84|
85|        if total_length > max_length:  # too long, truncate
86|            break
87|
88|        if word[-1] == ".":  # sentence end, truncate without "..."
89|            return " ".join(words[: i + 1])
90|
91|        if total_length == max_length and i != last_index:
92|            break  # not at sentence end, truncate with "..."
93|    else:
94|        return " ".join(words)  # no truncation needed
95|
96|    # Account for the length of the suffix.
97|    total_length += len("...")
98|
99|    # remove words until the length is short enough
100|    while i > 0:
101|        total_length -= len(words[i]) + (i > 0)
102|

111|class LazyFile:
112|    """A lazy file works like a regular file but it does not fully open
113|    the file but it does perform some basic checks early to see if the
114|    filename parameter does make sense.  This is useful for safely opening
115|    files for writing.
116|    """
117|
118|    def __init__(
119|        self,
120|        filename: str | os.PathLike[str],
121|        mode: str = "r",
122|        encoding: str | None = None,
123|        errors: str | None = "strict",
124|        atomic: bool = False,
125|    ):
126|        self.name: str = os.fspath(filename)
127|        self.mode = mode
128|        self.encoding = encoding
129|        self.errors = errors
130|        self.atomic = atomic
131|        self._f: IO[Any] | None
132|        self.should_close: bool
133|
134|        if self.name == "-":
135|            self._f, self.should_close = open_stream(filename, mode, encoding, errors)
136|        else:
137|            if "r" in mode:
138|                # Open and close the file in case we're opening it for
139|                # reading so that we can catch at least some errors in
140|                # some cases early.
141|                open(filename, mode).close()
142|            self._f = None
143|            self.should_close = True
144|
145|    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any:
146|        return getattr(self.open(), name)
147|
148|    def __repr__(self) -> str:
149|        if self._f is not None:
150|            return repr(self._f)
151|        return f"<unopened file '{format_filename(self.name)}' {self.mode}>"

153|    def open(self) -> IO[Any]:
154|        """Opens the file if it's not yet open.  This call might fail with
155|        a `FileError`.  Not handling this error will produce an error
156|        that Click shows.
157|        """
158|        if self._f is not None:
159|            return self._f
160|        try:
161|            rv, self.should_close = open_stream(
162|                self.name, self.mode, self.encoding, self.errors, atomic=self.atomic
163|            )
164|        except OSError as e:

167|            raise FileError(self.name, hint=e.strerror) from e

169|        return rv

171|    def close(self) -> None:
172|        """Closes the underlying file, no matter what."""
173|        if self._f is not None:
174|            self._f.close()

176|    def close_intelligently(self) -> None:
177|        """This function only closes the file if it was opened by the lazy
178|        file wrapper.  For instance this will never close stdin.
179|        """

199|def echo(
200|    message: Any | None = None,
201|    file: IO[Any] | None = None,
202|    nl: bool = True,
203|    err: bool = False,
204|    color: bool | None = None,
205|) -> None:
206|    """Print a message and newline to stdout or a file. This should be
207|    used instead of `print` because it provides better support
208|    for different data, files, and environments.
209|
210|    Compared to `print`, this does the following:
211|
212|    -   Ensures that the output encoding is not misconfigured on Linux.
213|    -   Supports Unicode in the Windows console.
214|    -   Supports writing to binary outputs, and supports writing bytes
215|        to text outputs.
216|    -   Supports colors and styles on Windows.
217|    -   Removes ANSI color and style codes if the output does not look
218|        like an interactive terminal.
219|    -   Always flushes the output.
220|    """
221|    if file is None:
222|        if err:
223|            file = _default_text_stderr()
224|        else:
225|            file = _default_text_stdout()
226|
227|        # There are no standard streams attached to write to. For example,
228|        # pythonw on Windows.
229|        if file is None:
230|            return
231|
232|    # Convert non bytes/text into the native string type.
233|    if message is not None and not isinstance(message, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
234|        out: str | bytes | bytearray | None = str(message)
235|    else:
236|        out = message
237|
238|    if nl:
239|        out = out or ""
240|        if isinstance(out, str):
241|            out += "\n"
242|        else:
243|            out += b"\n"
244|
245|    if not out:
246|        file.flush()
247|        return
248|
249|    # If there is a message and the value looks like bytes, we manually
250|    # need to find the binary stream and write the message in there.
251|    # This is done separately so that most stream types will work as you
252|    # would expect. Eg: you can write to StringIO for other cases.
253|    if isinstance(out, (bytes, bytearray)):
254|        binary_file = _find_binary_writer(file)
255|
256|        if binary_file is not None:
257|            file.flush()
258|            binary_file.write(out)
259|            binary_file.flush()
260|            return
261|
262|    # ANSI style code support. For no message or bytes, nothing happens.
263|    # When outputting to a file instead of a terminal, strip codes.
264|    else:
265|        color = resolve_color_default(color)
266|
267|        if should_strip_ansi(file, color):
268|            out = strip_ansi(out)
269|        elif WIN:

271|                file = auto_wrap_for_ansi(file, color)  # type: ignore[arg-type,call-arg]
272|            elif not color:
273|                out = strip_ansi(out)

275|    file.write(out)  # type: ignore[arg-type]

303|def format_filename(
304|    filename: str | bytes | os.PathLike[str] | os.PathLike[bytes],
305|    shorten: bool = False,
306|) -> str:
307|    """Format a filename as a string for display. Ensures the filename can be
308|    displayed by replacing any invalid bytes or surrogate escapes in the name
309|    with the replacement character ``�``.
310|
311|    Invalid bytes or surrogate escapes will raise an error when written to a
312|    stream with ``errors="strict"``. This will typically happen with ``stdout``
313|    when the locale is something like ``en_GB.UTF-8``.
314|
315|    Many scenarios *are* safe to write surrogates though, due to PEP 538 and
316|    PEP 540, including:
317|
318|    -   Writing to ``stderr``, which uses ``errors="backslashreplace"``.
319|    -   The system has ``LANG=C.UTF-8``, ``C``, or ``POSIX``. Python opens
320|        stdout and stderr with ``errors="surrogateescape"``.
321|    -   None of ``LANG/LC_*`` are set. Python assumes ``LANG=C.UTF-8``.
322|    -   Python is started in UTF-8 mode  with  ``PYTHONUTF8=1`` or ``-X utf8``.
323|        Python opens stdout and stderr with ``errors="surrogateescape"``.
324|    """
325|    if shorten:
326|        filename = os.path.basename(filename)
327|    else:
328|        filename = os.fspath(filename)
329|
330|    if isinstance(filename, bytes):
331|        filename = filename.decode(sys.getfilesystemencoding(), "replace")
332|    else:
333|        filename = filename.encode("utf-8", "surrogateescape").decode(
334|            "utf-8", "replace"
335|        )
336|
337|    return filename

342|    is to return whatever is most appropriate for the operating system.

353|    Unix (POSIX):

357|    Windows (not roaming):

378|class PacifyFlushWrapper:
379|    """This wrapper is used to catch and suppress BrokenPipeErrors resulting
380|    from ``.flush()`` being called on broken pipe during the shutdown/final-GC
381|    of the Python interpreter. Notably ``.flush()`` is always called on
382|    ``sys.stdout`` and ``sys.stderr``. So as to have minimal impact on any
383|    other cleanup code, and the case where the underlying file is not a broken
384|    pipe, all calls and attributes are proxied.
385|    """
386|
387|    def __init__(self, wrapped: IO[Any]) -> None:
388|        self.wrapped = wrapped
389|
390|    def flush(self) -> None:
391|        try:
392|            self.wrapped.flush()
393|        except OSError as e:  # pragma: no cover
394|            import errno
395|
396|            if e.errno != errno.EPIPE:
397|                raise
398|
399|    def __getattr__(self, attr: str) -> Any:
400|        return getattr(self.wrapped, attr)

403|def _detect_program_name(

405|) -> str:
406|    """Determine the command used to run the program, for use in help
407|    text. If a file or entry point was executed, the file name is
408|    returned. If ``python -m`` was used to execute a module or package,
409|    ``python -m name`` is returned.
410|
411|    This doesn't try to be too precise, the goal is to give a concise
412|    name for help text. Files are only shown as their name without the
413|    path. ``python`` is only shown for modules, and the full path to
414|    ``sys.executable`` is not shown.
415|    """
416|    if _main is None:
417|        _main = sys.modules["__main__"]
418|
419|    if not path:
420|        path = sys.argv[0]
421|

423|    # not exist if a setuptools script is installed as an egg. It may be
424|    # set incorrectly for entry points created with pip on Windows.
425|    # It is set to "" inside a Shiv or PEX zipapp.

429|        and not os.path.exists(path)
430|        and os.path.exists(f"{path}.exe")
431|    ):

433|        return os.path.basename(path)
434|
435|    # Executed a module, like "python -m example".
436|    # Rewritten by Python from "-m script" to "/path/to/script.py".
437|    # Need to look at main module to determine how it was executed.
438|    py_module = cast(str, _main.__package__)

440|
441|    # A submodule like "example.cli".
442|    if name != "__main__":
443|        py_module = f"{py_module}.{name}"
444|
445|    return f"python -m {py_module.lstrip('.')}"

283|    @contextmanager
284|    def scope(self, cleanup: bool = True) -> Iterator["Context"]:
285|        """This helper method can be used with the context object to promote
286|        it to the current thread local (see `get_current_context`).
287|        The default behavior of this is to invoke the cleanup functions which
288|        can be disabled by setting `cleanup` to `False`.  The cleanup
289|        functions are typically used for things such as closing file handles.

291|        If the cleanup is intended the context object can also be directly
292|        used as a context manager.

294|        if not cleanup:

297|            with self as rv:

300|            if not cleanup:

326|    def with_resource(self, context_manager: AbstractContextManager[V]) -> V:
327|        """Register a resource as if it were used in a ``with``
328|        statement. The resource will be cleaned up when the context is
329|        popped.

332|        resource's ``__enter__()`` method and returns the result. When
333|        the context is popped, it closes the stack, which calls the
334|        resource's ``__exit__()`` method.

337|        context manager, use `call_on_close`. Or use something
338|        from `contextlib` to turn it into a context manager first.

342|    def call_on_close(self, f: Callable[..., Any]) -> Callable[..., Any]:

346|        execution. Resources that support Python's context manager
347|        protocol which would be used in a ``with`` statement should be
348|        registered with `with_resource` instead.

358|    def _close_with_exception_info(
359|        self,
360|        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
361|        exc_value: BaseException | None,
362|        tb: TracebackType | None,
363|    ) -> bool | None:
364|        """Unwind the exit stack by calling its `__exit__` providing the exception
365|        information to allow for exception handling by the various resources registered

369|        # In case the context is reused, create a new exit stack.
370|        self._exit_stack = ExitStack()
371|
372|        return exit_result

503|class Command(ABC):
504|    """Commands are the basic building block of command line interfaces in
505|    Click.  A basic command handles command line parsing and might dispatch
506|    more parsing to commands nested below it.
507|    """
508|
509|    context_class: type[Context] = Context
510|    allow_extra_args = False
511|    allow_interspersed_args = True
512|    ignore_unknown_options = False
513|
514|    def __init__(
515|        self,
516|        name: str | None,
517|        context_settings: MutableMapping[str, Any] | None = None,
518|        callback: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
519|        params: list["Parameter"] | None = None,
520|        help: str | None = None,
521|        epilog: str | None = None,
522|        short_help: str | None = None,
523|        options_metavar: str | None = "[OPTIONS]",
524|        add_help_option: bool = True,
525|        no_args_is_help: bool = False,
526|        hidden: bool = False,
527|        deprecated: bool | str = False,
528|    ) -> None:
529|        self.name = name
530|
531|        if context_settings is None:
532|            context_settings = {}
533|
534|        self.context_settings: MutableMapping[str, Any] = context_settings
535|
536|        self.callback = callback
537|        self.params: list[Parameter] = params or []
538|        self.help = help
539|        self.epilog = epilog
540|        self.options_metavar = options_metavar
541|        self.short_help = short_help
542|        self.add_help_option = add_help_option
543|        self._help_option: TyperOption | None = None
544|        self.no_args_is_help = no_args_is_help
545|        self.hidden = hidden
546|        self.deprecated = deprecated
547|
548|    def __repr__(self) -> str:
549|        return f"<{self.__class__.__name__} {self.name}>"
550|
551|    def get_usage(self, ctx: Context) -> str:
552|        """Formats the usage line into a string and returns it."""
553|        formatter = ctx.make_formatter()
554|        self.format_usage(ctx, formatter)
555|        return formatter.getvalue().rstrip("\n")
556|
557|    def get_params(self, ctx: Context) -> list["Parameter"]:
558|        params = self.params
559|        help_option = self.get_help_option(ctx)
560|
561|        if help_option is not None:
562|            params = [*params, help_option]
563|
564|        return params
565|
566|    def format_usage(self, ctx: Context, formatter: HelpFormatter) -> None:
567|        """Writes the usage line into the formatter."""
568|        pieces = self.collect_usage_pieces(ctx)
569|        formatter.write_usage(ctx.command_path, " ".join(pieces))
570|
571|    def collect_usage_pieces(self, ctx: Context) -> list[str]:
572|        """Returns all the pieces that go into the usage line and returns
573|        it as a list of strings.
574|        """
575|        rv = [self.options_metavar] if self.options_metavar else []
576|
577|        for param in self.get_params(ctx):
578|            rv.extend(param.get_usage_pieces(ctx))
579|
580|        return rv
581|
582|    def get_help_option_names(self, ctx: Context) -> list[str]:
583|        """Returns the names for the help option."""
584|        all_names = set(ctx.help_option_names)
585|        for param in self.params:
586|            all_names.difference_update(param.opts)
587|            all_names.difference_update(param.secondary_opts)
588|        return list(all_names)
589|
590|    def get_help_option(self, ctx: Context) -> Union["TyperOption", None]:
591|        """Returns the help option object."""
592|        help_option_names = self.get_help_option_names(ctx)
593|
594|        if not help_option_names or not self.add_help_option:
595|            return None
596|
597|        # Cache the help option object in private _help_option attribute to
598|        # avoid creating it multiple times. Not doing this will break the
599|        # callback ordering by iter_params_for_processing(), which relies on
600|        # object comparison.
601|        if self._help_option is None:
602|            # Avoid circular import.
603|            from .decorators import help_option
604|
605|            # Apply help_option decorator and pop resulting option
606|            help_option(help_option_names)(self)
607|            self._help_option = cast("TyperOption", self.params.pop())
608|
609|        return self._help_option

611|    def make_parser(self, ctx: Context) -> _OptionParser:
612|        """Creates the underlying option parser for this command."""
613|        parser = _OptionParser(ctx)
614|        for param in self.get_params(ctx):
615|            param.add_to_parser(parser, ctx)
616|        return parser

618|    def get_help(self, ctx: Context) -> str:
619|        """Formats the help into a string and returns it."""
620|        formatter = ctx.make_formatter()
621|        self.format_help(ctx, formatter)
622|        return formatter.getvalue().rstrip("\n")

624|    def get_short_help_str(self, limit: int = 45) -> str:
625|        """Gets short help for the command or makes it by shortening the
626|        long help string.
627|        """
628|        if self.short_help:
629|            text = inspect.cleandoc(self.short_help)
630|        elif self.help:
631|            text = make_default_short_help(self.help, limit)
632|        else:
633|            text = ""
634|
635|        if self.deprecated:
636|            deprecated_message = (
637|                f"(DEPRECATED: {self.deprecated})"
638|                if isinstance(self.deprecated, str)
639|                else "(DEPRECATED)"
640|            )
641|            text = f"{text} {deprecated_message}"
642|
643|        return text.strip()

645|    def format_help(self, ctx: Context, formatter: HelpFormatter) -> None:
646|        """Writes the help into the formatter if it exists."""
647|        self.format_usage(ctx, formatter)
648|        self.format_help_text(ctx, formatter)
649|        self.format_options(ctx, formatter)
650|        self.format_epilog(ctx, formatter)

652|    def format_help_text(self, ctx: Context, formatter: HelpFormatter) -> None:
653|        """Writes the help text to the formatter if it exists."""
654|        if self.help is not None:
655|            # truncate the help text to the first form feed
656|            text = inspect.cleandoc(self.help).partition("\f")[0]
657|        else:
658|            text = ""
659|
660|        if self.deprecated:
661|            deprecated_message = (
662|                f"(DEPRECATED: {self.deprecated})"
663|                if isinstance(self.deprecated, str)
664|                else "(DEPRECATED)"
665|            )
666|            text = f"{text} {deprecated_message}"
667|
668|        if text:
669|            formatter.write_paragraph()
670|
671|            with formatter.indentation():

674|    @abstractmethod
675|    def format_options(self, ctx: Context, formatter: HelpFormatter) -> None:

678|    def format_epilog(self, ctx: Context, formatter: HelpFormatter) -> None:

687|    def make_context(
688|        self,
689|        info_name: str | None,
690|        args: list[str],
691|        parent: Context | None = None,
692|        **extra: Any,
693|    ) -> Context:
694|        """This function when given an info name and arguments will kick
695|        off the parsing and create a new `Context`.  It does not
696|        invoke the actual command callback though.
697|
698|        To quickly customize the context class used without overriding
699|        this method, set the `context_class` attribute.
700|        """
701|        for key, value in self.context_settings.items():
702|            if key not in extra:
703|                extra[key] = value
704|
705|        ctx = self.context_class(self, info_name=info_name, parent=parent, **extra)
706|
707|        with ctx.scope(cleanup=False):
708|            self.parse_args(ctx, args)
709|        return ctx
710|
711|    def parse_args(self, ctx: Context, args: list[str]) -> list[str]:
712|        if not args and self.no_args_is_help and not ctx.resilient_parsing:
713|            raise NoArgsIsHelpError(ctx)  # pragma: no cover
714|
715|        parser = self.make_parser(ctx)
716|        opts, args, param_order = parser.parse_args(args=args)
717|
718|        for param in iter_params_for_processing(param_order, self.get_params(ctx)):
719|            _, args = param.handle_parse_result(ctx, opts, args)
720|
721|        if args and not ctx.allow_extra_args and not ctx.resilient_parsing:
722|            extra_args = " ".join(_escape_control_characters(str(arg)) for arg in args)
723|            ctx.fail(f"Got unexpected extra argument(s) ({extra_args})")
724|
725|        ctx.args = args
726|        ctx._opt_prefixes.update(parser._opt_prefixes)
727|        return args
728|
729|    def invoke(self, ctx: Context) -> Any:
730|        """Given a context, this invokes the attached callback (if it exists)
731|        in the right way.
732|        """
733|        if self.deprecated:
734|            extra_message = (
735|                f" {self.deprecated}" if isinstance(self.deprecated, str) else ""
736|            )
737|            message = f"DeprecationWarning: The command {self.name!r} is deprecated.{extra_message}"
738|            echo(style(message, fg="red"), err=True)
739|
740|        if self.callback is not None:
741|            return ctx.invoke(self.callback, **ctx.params)

743|    def shell_complete(self, ctx: Context, incomplete: str) -> list["CompletionItem"]:
744|        """Return a list of completions for the incomplete value. Looks
745|        at the names of options and chained multi-commands.
746|
747|        Any command could be part of a chained multi-command, so sibling
748|        commands are valid at any point during command completion.
749|        """
750|        # avoid circular imports
751|        from .shell_completion import CompletionItem
752|
753|        results: list[CompletionItem] = []
754|
755|        if incomplete and not incomplete[0].isalnum():
756|            # avoid circular imports
757|            from ..core import TyperOption
758|
759|            for param in self.get_params(ctx):
760|                if (
761|                    not isinstance(param, TyperOption)
762|                    or param.hidden
763|                    or (
764|                        not param.multiple
765|                        and ctx.get_parameter_source(param.name)  # type: ignore
766|                        is ParameterSource.COMMANDLINE
767|                    )
768|                ):
769|                    continue
770|
771|                results.extend(
772|                    CompletionItem(name, help=param.help)
773|                    for name in [*param.opts, *param.secondary_opts]
774|                    if name.startswith(incomplete)
775|                )

172|    If `markup_mode` is `"markdown"`, parse as Markdown.

189|    *,
190|    obj: _click.Command | TyperGroup,
191|    markup_mode: MarkupModeStrict,
192|) -> Iterable[Markdown | Text]:
193|    """Build primary help text for a click command or group.

200|    if obj.deprecated:

207|    help_text = help_text.partition("\f")[0]
208|
209|    # Get the first paragraph
210|    first_line, *remaining_paragraphs = help_text.split("\n\n")
211|
212|    # Remove single linebreaks
213|    if markup_mode != MARKUP_MODE_MARKDOWN and not first_line.startswith("\b"):
214|        first_line = first_line.replace("\n", " ")

220|

224|        yield Text("")
225|        remaining_lines = _fix_linebreaks(remaining_paragraphs, markup_mode)
226|
227|        yield _make_rich_text(

275|    help_value: str | None = getattr(param, "help", None)
276|    if help_value:

290|                markup_mode=markup_mode,
291|            )
292|        )

295|    if envvar and getattr(param, "show_envvar", None):
296|        items.append(Text(ENVVAR_STRING.format(var_str), style=STYLE_OPTION_ENVVAR))

300|    if isinstance(param, (TyperOption, TyperArgument)):

308|                show_default_is_str=show_default_is_str,

555|def rich_format_help(
556|    *,
557|    obj: _click.Command | TyperGroup,
558|    ctx: _click.Context,
559|    markup_mode: MarkupModeStrict,
560|) -> None:
561|    """Print nicely formatted help text using rich.
562|
563|    Based on original code from rich-cli, by @willmcgugan.
564|    https://github.com/Textualize/rich-cli/blob/8a2767c7a340715fc6fbf4930ace717b9b2fc5e5/src/rich_cli/__main__.py#L162-L236
565|
566|    Replacement for the click function format_help().
567|    Takes a command or group and builds the help text output.
568|    """
569|    console = _get_rich_console()
570|
571|    # Print usage
572|    console.print(
573|        Padding(highlighter(obj.get_usage(ctx)), 1), style=STYLE_USAGE_COMMAND
574|    )
575|
576|    # Print command / group help if we have some
577|    if obj.help:
578|        # Print with some padding
579|        console.print(
580|            Padding(
581|                Align(
582|                    _get_help_text(
583|                        obj=obj,
584|                        markup_mode=markup_mode,
585|                    ),
586|                    pad=False,
587|                ),
588|                (0, 1, 1, 1),
589|            )
590|        )
591|    panel_to_arguments: defaultdict[str, list[TyperArgument]] = defaultdict(list)
592|    panel_to_options: defaultdict[str, list[TyperOption]] = defaultdict(list)
593|    for param in obj.get_params(ctx):
594|        # Skip if option is hidden
595|        if getattr(param, "hidden", False):
596|            continue
597|        if isinstance(param, TyperArgument):
598|            panel_name = (
599|                getattr(param, _RICH_HELP_PANEL_NAME, None) or ARGUMENTS_PANEL_TITLE
600|            )
601|            panel_to_arguments[panel_name].append(param)
602|        elif isinstance(param, TyperOption):
603|            panel_name = (
604|                getattr(param, _RICH_HELP_PANEL_NAME, None) or OPTIONS_PANEL_TITLE
605|            )
606|            panel_to_options[panel_name].append(param)
607|    default_arguments = panel_to_arguments.get(ARGUMENTS_PANEL_TITLE, [])
608|    _print_options_panel(
609|        name=ARGUMENTS_PANEL_TITLE,
610|        params=default_arguments,
611|        ctx=ctx,
612|        markup_mode=markup_mode,
613|        console=console,
614|    )
615|    for panel_name, arguments in panel_to_arguments.items():
616|        if panel_name == ARGUMENTS_PANEL_TITLE:
617|            # Already printed above
618|            continue
619|        _print_options_panel(
620|            name=panel_name,
621|            params=arguments,
622|            ctx=ctx,
623|            markup_mode=markup_mode,
624|            console=console,
625|        )
626|    default_options = panel_to_options.get(OPTIONS_PANEL_TITLE, [])
627|    _print_options_panel(
628|        name=OPTIONS_PANEL_TITLE,
629|        params=default_options,
630|        ctx=ctx,
631|        markup_mode=markup_mode,
632|        console=console,
633|    )
634|    for panel_name, options in panel_to_options.items():
635|        if panel_name == OPTIONS_PANEL_TITLE:
636|            # Already printed above
637|            continue
638|        _print_options_panel(
639|            name=panel_name,
640|            params=options,
641|            ctx=ctx,
642|            markup_mode=markup_mode,
643|            console=console,
644|        )
645|
646|    if isinstance(obj, TyperGroup):
647|        panel_to_commands: defaultdict[str, list[_click.Command]] = defaultdict(list)
648|        for command_name in obj.list_commands(ctx):
649|            command = obj.get_command(ctx, command_name)
650|            if command and not command.hidden:
651|                panel_name = (
652|                    getattr(command, _RICH_HELP_PANEL_NAME, None)
653|                    or COMMANDS_PANEL_TITLE
654|                )
655|                panel_to_commands[panel_name].append(command)
656|
657|        # Identify the longest command name in all panels
658|        max_cmd_len = max(
659|            [
660|                len(command.name or "")
661|                for commands in panel_to_commands.values()
662|                for command in commands
663|            ],
664|            default=0,
665|        )
666|
667|        # Print each command group panel
668|        default_commands = panel_to_commands.get(COMMANDS_PANEL_TITLE, [])
669|        _print_commands_panel(
670|            name=COMMANDS_PANEL_TITLE,
671|            commands=default_commands,
672|            markup_mode=markup_mode,
673|            console=console,
674|            cmd_len=max_cmd_len,
675|        )
676|        for panel_name, commands in panel_to_commands.items():
677|            if panel_name == COMMANDS_PANEL_TITLE:
678|                # Already printed above
679|                continue
680|            _print_commands_panel(
681|                name=panel_name,
682|                commands=commands,
683|                markup_mode=markup_mode,
684|                console=console,
685|                cmd_len=max_cmd_len,
686|            )
687|
688|    # Epilogue if we have it
689|    if obj.epilog:
690|        # Remove single linebreaks, replace double with single
691|        lines = obj.epilog.split("\n\n")
692|        epilogue = _fix_linebreaks(lines, markup_mode)
693|        epilogue_text = _make_rich_text(text=epilogue, markup_mode=markup_mode)
694|        console.print(Padding(Align(epilogue_text, pad=False), 1))

74|class BadParameter(UsageError):
75|    """An exception that formats out a standardized error message for a
76|    bad parameter.  This is useful when thrown from a callback or type as
77|    Click will attach contextual information to it (for instance, which
78|    parameter it is).
79|    """
80|
81|    def __init__(
82|        self,
83|        message: str,
84|        ctx: Union["Context", None] = None,
85|        param: Union["Parameter", None] = None,
86|        param_hint: Sequence[str] | str | None = None,
87|    ) -> None:
88|        super().__init__(message, ctx)
89|        self.param = param
90|        self.param_hint = param_hint
91|
92|    def format_message(self) -> str:
93|        if self.param_hint is not None:
94|            param_hint = self.param_hint
95|        elif self.param is not None:
96|            param_hint = self.param.get_error_hint(self.ctx)  # type: ignore
97|        else:
98|            return f"Invalid value: {self.message}"
99|
100|        hint = _join_param_hints(param_hint)
101|        return f"Invalid value for {hint}: {self.message}"

275|    def make_step(self, n_steps: int) -> None:
276|        self.pos += n_steps
277|        if self.length is not None and self.pos >= self.length:
278|            self.finished = True
279|
280|        if (time.time() - self.last_eta) < 1.0:
281|            return
282|
283|        self.last_eta = time.time()
284|
285|        # self.avg is a rolling list of length <= 7 of steps where steps are
286|        # defined as time elapsed divided by the total progress through
287|        # self.length.
288|        if self.pos:
289|            step = (time.time() - self.start) / self.pos
290|        else:
291|            step = time.time() - self.start
292|
293|        self.avg = self.avg[-6:] + [step]
294|
295|        self.eta_known = self.length is not None

297|    def update(self, n_steps: int) -> None:
298|        """Update the progress bar by advancing a specified number of steps."""
299|        self._completed_intervals += n_steps
300|
301|        if self._completed_intervals >= self.update_min_steps:
302|            self.make_step(self._completed_intervals)
303|            self.render_progress()

306|    def finish(self) -> None:
307|        self.eta_known = False
308|        self.current_item = None

311|    def generator(self) -> Iterator[V]:
312|        """Return a generator which yields the items added to the bar
313|        during construction, and updates the progress bar *after* the
314|        yielded block returns.
315|        """
316|        # WARNING: the iterator interface for `ProgressBar` relies on
317|        # this and only works because this is a simple generator which
318|        # doesn't create or manage additional state. If this function
319|        # changes, the impact should be evaluated both against
320|        # `iter(bar)` and `next(bar)`. `next()` in particular may call
321|        # `self.generator()` repeatedly, and this must remain safe in
322|        # order for that interface to work.
323|        if not self.entered:  # pragma: no cover
324|            raise RuntimeError("You need to use progress bars in a with block.")
325|
326|        if not self._is_atty:
327|            yield from self.iter
328|        else:
329|            for rv in self.iter:
330|                self.current_item = rv
331|
332|                # This allows show_item_func to be updated before the
333|                # item is processed. Only trigger at the beginning of
334|                # the update interval.
335|                if self._completed_intervals == 0:
336|                    self.render_progress()
337|
338|                yield rv
339|                self.update(1)
340|
341|            self.finish()
342|            self.render_progress()
